messages:
Samir Patel: heads up — Customer 'GreenCart' just filed that their checkout autocomplete started returning garbled tokens after our eu-west -> eu-standby failover. They see short, truncated outputs and token ids that don't map to words. billing spike too.
Maya Rao: ack. Which variant got served? any model ids in the logs?
Samir Patel: logs show main route wanted model=redwood-1.1-full v=2025-11-07 but standby responded with model=redwood-1-lite q=4bit v=2024-06-12. response headers: X-Served-Model: redwood-1-lite; X-Routed-From: eu-standby; X-Request-Id: rcpt_8421
eng-runtime-bot: [alert] automatic failover triggered: region=eu-west -> eu-standby due to host OOM. served_variant=redwood-1-lite (compatibility_check=FAILED)
Alex Kim: oh — compat check FAILED, but it still served? that shouldn't happen.
Nora Chen: Can you paste a minimal repro curl? Need input that shows tokenization mismatch.
Samir Patel: sure — here's a sanitized repro we gave the customer:

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-***" -H "X-Region-Preference: eu-west" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1-full","prompt":"Translate to fr: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.","max_tokens":60}'

Response snippet:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Served-Model: redwood-1-lite
{"id":"gen_123","choices":[{"text":"\u0002\u00a1Le renard...","finish_reason":"length"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":12,"completion_tokens":4}}

notice invalid chars and very short completion.
Maya Rao: thanks. Also saw customer billing increased — they retried a bunch after getting bad output, so cost comp request inbound.
support-oncall: escalation filed -> TICKET-3921. Marked severity=P2 and asked for interim mitigation from runtime. Customer living invoice hold requested.
Alex Kim: immediate mitigation options: 1) force-route customer to hosted region (bypass standby) by setting routing.strict=true for that account, or 2) pin model_version explicitly in the backend so standby can't substitute a different architecture variant.
Nora Chen: eng-runtime, can you confirm why compatibility_check failed but failover still served incompatible variant? we expect fallback to block if tokenizer/vocab mismatches.
Alex Kim: adding logs: failure is at routing decision, compat check is async and may return after request is already routed. There's a race on standby admission during surge.
eng-runtime-bot: [note] race window observed: 300-450ms between route assignment and compat verification. If standby node answers before verification completes, it may serve.
Samir Patel: customer provided example token ids: [312, 5, 99999] where 99999 isn't in current vocab. that's indicative of different tokenizer or quantized remap.
Maya Rao: eng-ml — is the lite variant using a legacy tokenizer or a different vocab table?
Alex Kim (eng-runtime): eng-ml please confirm. If vocab differs, we should block variant substitution at router level until a compatibility matrix check passes.
Nora Chen (eng-ml): confirmed — redwood-1-lite uses legacy bytepair vocab with different token id mapping; it's an intentionally smaller architecture, not compatible for direct substitution. We have heuristics but they weren't enforced for standby in some clusters.
Samir Patel: immediate customer-facing response sent: "we see a failover to a lower-capability variant; we've applied a safe route to keep you on your pinned model while we remediate; refund in progress; engineering investigating." They want timeline.
Alex Kim: short-term fixes: 1) rollback standby routing policy for eu-standby cluster -> disable automatic standby selection for production tenants for 24h; 2) push hotfix to router to wait for compat-check before accepting first byte from standby (adds ~20-40ms but prevents mismatch);
eng-runtime-bot: [deploy] hotfix branch created: fix/compat-block-accept. QA run scheduled.
Nora Chen (eng-ml): longer term: add a per-model semantic compatibility fingerprint (vocab_hash + arch_sig) to route table and enforce exact-match or approved-variants only. Also add an alert if served_variant != requested_family.
Maya Rao: can we also add a migration tool to map outputs from lite->full where possible? might reduce customer pain for some prompts.
Nora Chen (eng-ml): possible but brittle. prefer blocking wrong variant. mapping only for safe, idempotent transforms.
support-oncall: update: customer accepted temporary routing override. They've paused retries. Billing team looped for compensation.
Samir Patel: owners/tasks:
- Alex Kim (eng-runtime): roll forward compat-block hotfix, coordinate rollback of eu-standby auto-select (ETA 2h)
- Nora Chen (eng-ml): produce compatibility matrix and short doc for allowed substitutes (ETA 48h)
- Maya Rao (support): keep customer updated + billing comp (ongoing)
- Samir Patel: prepare incident SWIFT postmortem (due EOD tomorrow)
Maya Rao: +1 on postmortem. Also add test in CI that simulates failover and verifies tokenizer hash checks.
Alex Kim: will queue the CI test. posting links to the branch and ticket in TICKET-3921.
Samir Patel: thanks all — pinging here when hotfix is live.
eng-runtime-bot: [status] compat-block hotfix deployed to eu-standby canary at 2795556675. Observed requests now blocked until compat confirmed.
Samir Patel: can confirm customer reported normal outputs after override, closing immediate incident. moving to follow-up for root cause and billing reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
